items.title: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka to remain in custody until October 21
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday, October 19, extended the judicial custody of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka by two days over an alleged breach of peace bonds. They will remain in custody until their next hearing on October 21. The Delhi police had sought a five-day extension, alleging that the two had breached bonds they furnished on October 11 by calling on people to gather at Jantar Mantar. Police said the site had been de-notified as an official protest venue and alleged that Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka had used social media to mobilise people for demonstrations at other non-designated locations, including Connaught Place, Live Law reported. The CJP leaders were initially detained at an airport on October 10, ahead of protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over massive irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. They were released that day after furnishing peace bonds of Rs 50,000 each. A vacation Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana of the apex court will hear the plea on October 21. That is also the last date for withdrawal of candidature. Polling is scheduled for October 28. The party first moved the High Court on October 10, before the polls were notified, seeking secure additional nomination centres. A single-judge dismissed that plea on October 15. Subsequently, it moved the High Court flagging violence at nomination centres and seeking extension of deadline to file nominations. On October 18, a division bench of the High Court comprising Justices Ninala Jayasurya and Purushottam Kumar Chintalapudi rejected the party's plea for a one-day extension to file nominations.
